signals.title: NZD/JPY — G10 Bilateral Theme + Monetary Divergence
signals.text: NZD/JPY trades at 85.50 as the JPY outperformance theme dominates G10 flows following hawkish BoJ rhetoric. BoJ holds at 1.0%. The 4.217% leader-to-laggard spread between JPY and NZD reflects a massive shift in carry-unwind dynamics, with NZD/USD holding below its SMA20 of 0.5910 and USD/JPY testing its SMA200 at 158.45. Despite a +335bp nominal carry advantage for AUD/JPY and similar spreads for NZD, the BoJ’s policy pivot risk is forcing a disorderly exit from yen-funded carry trades. Trade bias: Bearish NZD/JPY; JPY outperformance theme remains the dominant G10 driver. Catalyst: BoJ meeting 18 Sep — hike bias active. Risk: BoJ fails to deliver a hawkish signal, allowing the carry trade to restabilize.

signals.title: USD/JPY — BoJ Policy Repricing + Options Skew
signals.text: USD/JPY at 155.57 as Governor Ueda confirms rate hikes are on the table for the September meeting, prompting a 1-month high in the Yen. The 25d RR at -2.64 shows a massive put skew, signaling that the options market is paying a significant premium for USD/JPY downside protection despite a 275bp Fed-BoJ carry advantage. Interestingly, IV at 7.2% remains well below HV30 of 12.1%, resulting in a -4.9% VRP that indicates the options market may still be underpricing the realized volatility of this policy-driven move. Technicals show USD/JPY has decisively broken below its SMA20/50 cluster (159.17/160.71) and is now testing SMA200 support at 158.45 on a daily close basis. Trade bias: Bearish USD/JPY; hawkish BoJ shift overpowers the carry advantage. Catalyst: BoJ meeting 18 Sep — hike bias active. Risk: Fed surprises hawkish on 16 Sep, widening the yield gap and stalling the JPY rally.

signals.title: AUD/USD — Positioning Extreme + Retail Divergence
signals.text: AUD/USD at 0.7199 is testing the upper boundaries of its current range as speculative and retail positioning reach opposing extremes. COT LF net long sits at +53,578 (pctl 95, z +1.92), marking a crowded institutional long that historically caps near-term upside. In direct contrast, retail sentiment is 86% short, suggesting a major institutional-retail divergence that often leads to late-trend volatility. While the 69bp AONIA-SOFR carry premium supports AUD, the crowded spec long remains vulnerable to a sharp unwind if US yields catch a bid. Trade bias: Neutral/range AUD/USD; crowded spec longs limit upside despite retail fading the trend. Catalyst: US CPI next week. Risk: Retail capitulation leads to one final squeeze toward 0.7300.

signals.title: GBP/USD — Elevated Vol Premium + BoE Caution
signals.text: GBP/USD at 1.3535 faces increased two-way risk as BoE's Pill notes that recent geopolitical tensions have not de-anchored inflation expectations while downplaying aggressive hike paths. The options market is pricing in significant tail risk with a VRP of +6.2% (IV 11.0% vs HV30 4.8%), the highest premium in the G10 complex. This elevated hedging demand suggests traders are bracing for a volatility spike despite GBP's relatively neutral 0bp carry spread vs the Fed. Technically, Cable is holding below its SMA20 at 1.3550, with the SMA50/200 cluster at 1.3442/1.3444 providing the next major support zone. Trade bias: Neutral GBP/USD; elevated vol premium suggests market caution ahead of central bank meetings. Catalyst: ECB meeting 10 Sep. Risk: Geopolitical escalation in the Middle East drives a broad flight to USD.

signals.title: USD/NOK — ESI Outperformance vs Retail Longs
signals.text: USD/NOK at 9.311 reflects a strengthening Krone supported by a dominant Economic Surprise Index (ESI) of +89.4, the highest in G10. The Norges Bank remains on a hawkish footing with a 4.25% policy rate and a positive real rate of +1.57%, while retail sentiment sits at an extreme 100% long USD/NOK. This retail extreme is fading a structurally sound NOK move backed by consistent data beats and supportive energy prices. Technically, the pair remains in a clear downtrend, trading below its SMA20/50/200 cluster. Trade bias: Bearish USD/NOK; retail extreme provides contrarian support for NOK strength. Catalyst: Norges Bank meeting 24 Sep — hike bias active. Risk: WTI crude oil prices drop below $85, weakening the NOK's terms-of-trade support.
